no_lever.wanted: "Its Shellshockers and Mausers shell the turrets at spot_98 from their own reach, the Overwatch (armhlt) first, then the Beamers, then the Sentry, then his resurrection bots" (also 9:03, 11:25, 12:45, 13:43; commander 13:51 'Shell his resurrection bots too')
no_lever.why_no_lever: The shell move is a fight-move to a standoff point (execute.rs Order::Shell): it fires only at what is in sight, has no attack-ground on a remembered building and no target order. Artillery did 0 damage to turrets from 13:41 to 16:20 and first hit Beamers after they came into sight.

no_lever.wanted: "Its Blitzes stand at spot_116 as the screen in front of the Shellshockers and never walk into the reach of the turrets at spot_98" (also 9:03, 9:49, 11:25)
no_lever.why_no_lever: No move puts a group's artillery at its reach and its screen at a named place or outside a turret's reach: the shell move fixes the screen at 0.55 x the artillery's reach from the target. Opus found the workaround at 16:50 (hold the whole group at a marked siege_line).

no_lever.wanted: march for group_E's body walking to spot_116, while new soldiers from the plants join it from home
no_lever.why_no_lever: march waits for every member, joiners walking from home included; it cannot be scoped to the body, so the only choice was to drop it.

A list step with an id is read as building that type; a builder that cannot build the type skips it, so a list cannot send tier-1 builders to help a tier-2 frame (only the packet's help moves can, once the frame stands).
